sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A service that tries to re-identify an anonymous profile before it is published, with several models and code.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Try to find the person first; six steps; several models alone; the truth sealed; browser or session.

sections.label: The question
sections.line: Can a profile be reverse-engineered? Research shows models infer attributes with up to 85% accuracy.

sections.label: The team
sections.line: Extract, profile, vouchers, narrow, correlate in code, rewrite.

sections.label: Several models, each alone
sections.line: Claude, Mistral, DeepSeek and a local model guess independently; agreement means risk.

sections.label: The truth stays sealed
sections.line: The owner's real details stay sealed and only code compares guesses; the draft is public anyway.

sections.label: The report
sections.line: Risk by attribute, what gave it away, how narrow, what to change; saved without the truth.

sections.label: Where it runs
sections.line: In a Claude session, in the browser with the owner's keys, or on the device.

sections.label: Who would use it
sections.line: Anyone publishing something anonymous; a free self-check and a paid review.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not built; a pass is no guarantee; narrowing is an estimate.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: My thinking on 21 November 2026 and the Beyond Memorization paper.
